originalTitle: The 2.5-hour AI-generated Odyssey movie is 2.5 hours too long
summary: Christopher Nolan's engrossing take on The Odyssey dominated at the box office and spurred a newfound interest in classic literature among filmgoers. content: Christopher Nolan’s engrossing take on The Odyssey dominated at the box office and spurred a newfound interest in classic literature among filmgoers. But a new retelling of the story made entirely with AI is so bad that it might just make viewers hate the original tale altogether. The new film, called Odysseus: The Fall, comes via AI firm Fountain 0 and is written and directed by company cofounder Ash Koosha, who also lent his likeness to the title character and created all of the music. (The film’s credits are very short.) The studio’s only previous work is an AI film called Dreams of Violets that made it into Tribeca earlier this year. The Fall is, on its face, a much more ambitious project, billed as “the first completely AI generated film produced at the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.” In reality, it’s nothing close to “the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.” That may not necessarily be surprising, but after watching the entire 2.5-hour production I nonetheless found myself constantly surprised by just how much worse things could get. The Fall is the opposite of a glimpse at the future of AI filmmaking — it’ll make you wonder if there’s really any future in it at all. The movie is available to rent now for $9.99 and, as far as I can tell, you can only watch it via a web browser. In order to view it on my living room TV I had to mirror the screen from my phone, which is not exactly IMAX in 70mm. Things didn’t get much better once I pressed play. The Fall is plagued by two main issues. The first is consistency. The world of the film is constantly morphing, to the point that it’s incredibly distracting. The height of the cyclops that traps Odysseus and his men changes from shot to shot, waves move in the opposite direction of the wind, mouths don’t match the words spoken (and sometimes they move without producing a sound at all), and oars bend and twist as sailors row. In one scene a huge fleet of boats is racing through the ocean and one of them is inexplicably moving sideways. The AI-produced voice-overs can be incomprehensible, and at various points the names of both Odysseus and Zeus are pronounced wrong. If it were just the odd hiccup it might be understandable, but there are so many faults in The Fall that it can be hard to focus on anything else. I watched the movie with my 13-year-old kid and it basically became a game of finding the weirdest mistakes. I noticed that a sword magically turned into a dagger, and then she one-upped me by spotting an alien carcass roasting over a spit. The Fall seems like a film designed to prove why script supervisors exist. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NZ2VI7dQ91A] The thing is, while all of the AI-induced errors are distracting, they’re also the most entertaining part of the movie. There isn’t really much to distract from in The Fall because it is so dull. Because current AI models are really only capable of generating scenes that last a few seconds, the movie feels like a disjointed collection of moments from the odyssey that have been stitched together with little rhyme or reason. If you didn’t already know the story going into this, I don’t think you’d have any idea of what was going on, because the film explains very little. You don’t even learn about Penelope’s suitors until the movie is almost over. I also can’t think of a single aspect of The Fall that feels improved because of AI. The “acting” is bafflingly bad, with characters pausing for seconds at a time for no apparent reason and bursts of laughter that jolt you out of nowhere. There’s no weight to the action, as if this takes place in a world where things like physics and gravity are suggestions rather than constants. Similarly, there aren’t any cool or impressive effects that wouldn’t be possible without the technology. The monsters look like shabby stop-motion creatures from the 1930s, which is all the weirder when they’re put beside the smooth, hyperreal human characters that AI spews out. It’s not just jarring, it’s boring and ugly. Koosha claims that he adapted this story because he “always felt passionately about Homer’s epic tale since [he] originally read it years ago.” It seems much more likely that he’s trying to skate by on the hype and energy created by Nolan’s film, turning AI slop into a modern-day iteration of direct-to-video cash grabs. But this also puts the film at an incredible disadvantage from the very beginning, inviting comparisons to one of the most critically and commercially successful movies of the last few years, one that was especially beloved because of the director’s insistence on human craftsmanship. Nolan is someone who cares deeply about film, and his passion and enthusiasm is why stars want to work with him and viewers flock the theaters to see his movies. The existence of The Fall, meanwhile, shows utter contempt for the medium, attempting to boil the work of hundreds of skilled workers into slop produced by a tiny team. It’s so terrible it’ll make you appreciate human-made art all the more.
chineseTitle: AI 生成的 2.5 小时奥德赛电影太长了 2.5 小时
chineseSummary: 克里斯托弗·诺兰对《奥德赛》的引人入胜的演绎在票房上占据了主导地位，并激发了电影观众对古典文学的新兴趣。但完全用人工智能重新讲述这个故事实在是太糟糕了，以至于可能会让观众完全讨厌原来的故事。这部名为《奥德修斯：堕落》的新电影即将上映 […]
chineseContent: 克里斯托弗·诺兰对《奥德赛》的引人入胜的演绎在票房上占据了主导地位，并激发了电影观众对古典文学的新兴趣。但完全用人工智能重新讲述这个故事实在是太糟糕了，以至于可能会让观众完全讨厌原来的故事。这部名为《奥德修斯：堕落》的新电影由人工智能公司 Fountain 0 制作，由该公司联合创始人 Ash Koosha 编写和导演，他也将自己的肖像借给了片名角色并创作了所有音乐。 （这部电影的片尾字幕非常短。）该工作室之前唯一的一部作品是一部名为《紫罗兰之梦》的人工智能电影，该电影于今年早些时候在翠贝卡上映。从表面上看，《堕落》是一个更加雄心勃勃的项目，被宣传为“第一部完全由人工智能生成的好莱坞大片级别的电影”。事实上，这远不及“好莱坞大片的水平”。这可能并不令人惊讶，但在看完整个 2.5 小时的制作后，我仍然发现自己不断惊讶于事情会变得多么糟糕。 《秋天》与对人工智能电影制作未来的一瞥相反——它会让你怀疑它是否真的有未来。这部电影现在可以以 9.99 美元的价格租借，据我所知，你只能通过网络浏览器观看。为了在客厅电视上观看它，我必须通过手机镜像屏幕，这并不完全是 70 毫米的 IMAX。当我按下播放按钮后，情况并没有好转。秋天受到两个主要问题的困扰。首先是一致性。电影的世界在不断变化，以至于令人难以置信地分散注意力。困住奥德修斯和他的部下的独眼巨人的高度随着镜头的变化而变化，波浪向与风相反的方向移动，嘴巴与“sp”一词不符
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
